raw_response:
I farm only 7 mu, so I cannot spread myself too much. Same as before, I will keep the wheat-maize land on 5 mu, because that gives grain in two seasons and feels safer. The other 2 mu I will put in peanut. Peanut brings cash if the price is decent, but I do not want too much of it because it needs more watching and the family is not always at home since some people work outside.

For wheat, I mostly do what has worked on my land. If I starve the field, the wheat stays thin, so I will still put fertilizer, but not too heavy because fertilizer and water both cost money. I will give one base dressing before sowing and then one more when the wheat starts to rise fast in spring. Water from the well is available, but pumping costs money, so I will use it at the important times, not carelessly. After wheat harvest, maize must go in quickly. There is no time to fuss. I will clear the field fast, do light tillage or direct sow if I can get help, and plant hybrid maize right away. For peanut, I will keep it simpler, use less fertilizer than wheat, and water only if it turns too dry. I am not chasing the highest yield, I just want a steady harvest and not too much cash pressure.

I do not dare spend too much on inputs because money is tight and some family members work off-farm, but I also do not want to cut fertilizer too hard and lose yield.
